source_evidence.anchor: Section 2.1, equations (2.2)-(2.4), and the paragraph defining the unsubscripted norm
source_evidence.observation: A BLR representation has p block rows and columns, blocks of order b, and n = pb. Off-diagonal blocks are low-rank approximations. A local threshold uses β_ij = ||A_ij||, while a global threshold uses β_ij = ||A||. The unsubscripted matrix norm is the Frobenius norm.

source_evidence.anchor: Section 2.2, equation (2.5) and the definition of γ_k
source_evidence.observation: The analysis uses fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + δ), |δ| <= u, for op in {+, -, ×, /}. It defines γ_k = ku/(1-ku) when ku < 1, including for non-integer k.

Rounding errors in truncated-SVD compression are ignored: a computed low-rank block satisfies A_tilde_ij = A_ij + ΔA_ij with ||ΔA_ij|| <= εβ_ij. The standing analysis assumes u is safely smaller than ε.
The symbol r denotes the BLR rank of the LU factors, namely the largest rank among their off-diagonal blocks. It depends on the matrix and threshold and is not a tunable parameter.

Algorithm 1 is the left-looking update-factor-compress (UFC) execution: each block row and column is updated, factored, and then its off-diagonal factor blocks are compressed. Its factorization theorem is conditional on the algorithm running to completion.

For UFC, the subsequent simplified bounds use scaled local or global thresholds. The scaled choices remove diagonal-factor norms from the truncation bound and give coefficients 1 and p without intermediate recompressions.

Table 1 gives ξ_p as 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) for, respectively: local/no recompression, global/no recompression, local/with recompressions, and global/with recompressions. Theorem 4.2 gives the UFC factorization bound, conditional on nonsingularity and running to completion.

Algorithm 2 is update-compress-factor (UCF): updated off-diagonal blocks are compressed before factorization. Theorem 4.3 gives the corresponding factorization guarantee for a nonsingular matrix when the algorithm runs to completion.

The BLR triangular-solve result constructs simultaneous perturbations of the triangular matrix and right-hand side, with ||ΔT_tilde|| <= γ_c||T_tilde|| and ||Δv|| <= γ_p||v||. Its displayed block solve is the forward ordering for a lower-triangular matrix.

For factors produced by Algorithm 1 or 2 and the computed solution x_hat, Theorem 4.5 states (A + ΔA)x_hat = v + Δv, ||ΔA|| <= (ξ_p ε + γ_p)||A|| + γ_3c||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(uε), and ||Δv|| <= γ_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), where c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p.

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Theorem 4.5, exact perturbation products
source_evidence.observation: Before normwise simplification, the aggregate matrix perturbation is the factorization perturbation plus ΔL_tilde U_tilde + L_tilde ΔU_tilde + ΔL_tilde ΔU_tilde. The aggregate right-hand-side perturbation is the first-solve right-hand-side perturbation plus L_tilde Δy_hat + ΔL_tilde Δy_hat.

binders: Theorem 4.5 explicitly introduces A_tilde in R^(n×n) as a pb-by-pb BLR matrix and v in R^n; Section 2.1 supplies n = pb and the p-by-p block partition with blocks of order b. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening; PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, equations (2.2)-(2.4)]

The exact/original matrix symbol A appears in equations (4.23)-(4.24) and in the proof, although the theorem's local opening binds A_tilde rather than A. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 and equations (4.23)-(4.24)]

L_tilde and U_tilde are computed BLR LU factors produced by Algorithm 1 or Algorithm 2; y_hat and x_hat are the computed intermediate and final triangular-solve results. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 and proof opening; PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, triangular-solve perturbation equations]

The parameter r is the maximum off-diagonal block rank of the computed LU factors, and c is fixed in Theorem 4.5 as c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, opening of Section 4; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, text after equation (4.25)]
The threshold coefficient ξ_p is selected from Table 1 according to local versus global compression and absence versus presence of intermediate recompressions. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]

For each admissible input, parameter choice, successful factorization execution, and resulting x_hat, the standard perturbation reading of (4.23) is that aggregate perturbations ΔA and Δv exist after the computation. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.23); PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, construction of ΔA' and Δv']
hypotheses: The system described in the theorem is A_tilde x = v and is solved in the order L_tilde y = v followed by U_tilde x = y. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening]
The factors must be computed by either Algorithm 1 (UFC) or Algorithm 2 (UCF); no other factorization algorithm is named in the theorem. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening]

The factorization results invoked in the proof require the original matrix to be nonsingular and the selected factorization algorithm to run to completion. These conditions are explicit in Theorems 4.2 and 4.3 but not repeated verbatim in Theorem 4.5. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof invocation]

The lower and upper triangular solves must themselves be executable; the proof applies Theorem 4.4 to L_tilde and analogously to U_tilde. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, proof of Theorem 4.5]

Compression obeys Assumption 2.1: each truncated-SVD block error has norm at most εβ_ij, compression arithmetic is treated as exact apart from that truncation error, and u is safely smaller than ε. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1 and following paragraph]

Floating-point operations obey the standard relative-error model, and every used γ_k requires ku < 1. In particular, the displayed γ_p and γ_3c require pu < 1 and 3cu < 1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5) and definition of γ_k; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.24)-(4.25)]

The threshold and recompression variant must match the chosen ξ_p value in Table 1. For UFC, the preceding derivation uses the scaled local/global choices of equations (4.13)-(4.14). [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, equations (4.13)-(4.15); PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1 and Theorem 4.2]
conclusions: There are aggregate perturbations satisfying the exact mixed backward equation (A + ΔA)x_hat = v + Δv. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.23)]

The matrix perturbation satisfies ||ΔA|| <= (ξ_p ε + γ_p)||A|| + γ_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(uε). The factor (ξ_p ε + γ_p) multiplies the whole norm ||A||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24)]

The right-hand-side perturbation satisfies ||Δv|| <= γ_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2). The γ_p factor multiplies both displayed terms inside the parentheses. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.25)]

With distinct names for internal and final perturbations, the proof's exact matrix composition is ΔA_sys = ΔA_fac + ΔL_tilde U_tilde + L_tilde ΔU_tilde + ΔL_tilde ΔU_tilde. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, first exact product expansion in the proof of Theorem 4.5]

The proof's exact right-hand-side composition is Δv_sys = δv + L_tilde δy_hat + ΔL_tilde δy_hat, where δv comes from the first triangular solve and δy_hat from the second. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, second exact product expansion in the proof of Theorem 4.5]
definitions_and_conventions: A BLR matrix has p block rows and columns, blocks of order b, and total order n = pb; its off-diagonal blocks are represented in low-rank form. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, equations (2.2)-(2.4)]
A local compression threshold uses β_ij = ||A_ij|| and a global threshold uses β_ij = ||A||. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, equation (2.4) and following paragraph]

For UFC's simplified factorization bound, 'local' and 'global' inherit the scaled choices leading to ||G|| <= ε||A|| and ||G|| <= pε||A|| in equations (4.13) and (4.14). [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, equations (4.13)-(4.15)]

Table 1 defines ξ_p as follows: local without recompressions, 1; global without recompressions, p; local with recompressions, p; global with recompressions, p^2/sqrt(6). [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]

A tilde marks BLR representations or computed BLR factors, while a hat marks computed triangular-solve results in the displayed theorem and proof notation. [PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, Theorem 4.5 and its proof]
γ_k means ku/(1-ku), defined only when ku < 1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, definition following equation (2.5)]
implicit_context: Section 2.1 uses A for an original dense matrix and A_tilde for its BLR representation; this is the natural inherited interpretation of the otherwise unbound A in (4.23)-(4.24), but Theorem 4.5 does not restate that relationship locally. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, equations (2.1)-(2.4); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

The quantifier order is input and algorithm parameters first, then a successful computed execution, then existence of perturbations describing that particular computed x_hat. [PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, Theorem 4.5 and construction of ΔA' and Δv']

Nonsingularity and running to completion are inherited through the proof's invocation of Theorems 4.2 and 4.3. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof of Theorem 4.5]

The displayed block ordering in Theorem 4.4 is forward substitution for a lower-triangular matrix; the upper-triangular application in Theorem 4.5 is introduced only by 'Similarly'. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, upper-solve equation]

No particular pivoting policy is imposed by Theorem 4.5; factor growth remains visible through ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, discussion preceding Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, UCF pivoting discussion; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The permitted factorization executions are Algorithm 1, the left-looking UFC order update-factor-compress, and Algorithm 2, the UCF order update-compress-factor. Intermediate recompressions during factorization select the corresponding Table 1 row. After factorization, the computation solves with L_tilde and then U_tilde. Theorem 4.5 obtains the factor perturbation from Theorem 4.2 or 4.3 and each solve perturbation from Theorem 4.4; its proof explicitly uses the computed y_hat as the upper solve's right-hand side. [PDF p. 13, printed p. 963, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1 and Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 4.3; PDF pp. 23-25, printed pp. 973-975, Theorems 4.4-4.5]
numerical_model: All basic real floating-point operations use fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + δ), |δ| <= u. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5)]
γ_k = ku/(1-ku) for ku < 1, and the paper permits non-integer indices such as c and 3c. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, paragraph following equation (2.5)]
Low-rank compression is modeled by a normwise truncated-SVD error ||ΔA_ij|| <= εβ_ij, while rounding error in constructing that approximation is ignored. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]
The standing regime is u safely smaller than ε, which is used when mixed and higher-order terms are summarized. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, paragraph following Assumption 2.1]
error_notions: Equation (4.23) is a simultaneous, normwise backward-error statement perturbing both the matrix and the right-hand side; it is not a forward-error bound for x_hat. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.23)-(4.25)]

The matrix bound separates an LR truncation contribution ξ_p ε||A||, ordinary floating-point contributions γ_p||A|| and γ_3c||L_tilde||||U_tilde||, and a mixed O(uε) remainder. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24)]
The right-hand-side backward error is not bounded solely relative to ||v||: it also contains ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.25)]
The factor-growth dependence is explicit through ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||, so the theorem does not assert a factor-independent small relative error. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.24)-(4.25)]
norms: Every unsubscripted matrix norm in the analysis is the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, paragraph defining the unsubscripted norm]
For vectors, the same sum-of-squares convention is the Euclidean norm. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Frobenius norm definition; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, vector terms in equation (4.25)]
The Frobenius norm is used as a submultiplicative norm and satisfies the blockwise identity ||A||^2 = sum_ij ||A_ij||^2. [PDF pp. 3-4, printed pp. 953-954, norm-properties discussion]
constants_and_indexing: The final theorem uses c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p and γ_(3c), with no omitted offset in c. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24) and the following line]

The triangular-solve theorem itself uses b + r^(3/2) + p; Theorem 4.5 adopts the larger factorization constant b + 2r^(3/2) + p as a common c. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
The lower-triangular block solve displayed in Theorem 4.4 uses x_i = x((i-1)b+1:ib) and sums prior blocks j = 1 through i-1. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4]
The four ξ_p values are exactly 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) in the Table 1 row-column order local/no, global/no, local/with, global/with recompressions. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
The rank r is the maximum off-diagonal rank of the LU factors, not necessarily the rank of the input BLR blocks. [PDF p. 12, printed p. 962, opening of Section 4]
higher_order_terms: Equation (4.24) retains an unspecified O(uε) term; it must not be dropped or replaced by zero. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24)]
Equation (4.25) retains an unspecified O(u^2) term; it must not be dropped or replaced by zero. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.25)]
Before simplification, the exact matrix product contains the cross term ΔL_tilde ΔU_tilde. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, first product expansion]
Before simplification, the exact right-hand-side product contains the cross term ΔL_tilde Δy_hat. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, second product expansion]

The theorem does not provide explicit constants or a quantified validity range for either big-O remainder beyond the standing floating-point and u << ε assumptions. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, standing assumption; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.24)-(4.25)]
exceptional_values: The factorization guarantee is conditional on running to completion, so breakdown or a zero pivot is outside the stated conclusion. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]
The invoked factorization theorems assume A is nonsingular. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]

The γ quantities are defined only when their denominators are positive; the final bound therefore inherits pu < 1 and 3cu < 1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, definition of γ_k; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.24)-(4.25)]
The standard model shown in equation (2.5) gives no separate treatment of overflow, underflow, NaNs, or infinities. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5)]

undebatable_constraints: The principal conclusion must retain simultaneous perturbations on both sides: (A + ΔA)x_hat = v + Δv. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.23)]
The first term of the matrix bound is (ξ_p ε + γ_p)||A||, not ξ_p ε + γ_p||A||. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24)]
The factor term is γ_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| with c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24) and following line]
The right-hand-side bound is γ_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), with both displayed terms inside γ_p's parentheses. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.25)]
The ξ_p table must preserve all four cases: 1, p, p, and p^2/sqrt(6) for local/no, global/no, local/with, and global/with recompressions. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1]
Only UFC Algorithm 1 and UCF Algorithm 2 are named as permitted factorization executions in Theorem 4.5. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 opening]

The inherited factorization guarantee is conditional on a nonsingular matrix and the selected algorithm running to completion. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3]
All displayed norm bounds are Frobenius-norm, normwise statements. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, norm convention; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.24)-(4.25)]
The exact aggregate matrix perturbation must preserve ΔL_tilde U_tilde, L_tilde ΔU_tilde, and ΔL_tilde ΔU_tilde. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, first exact perturbation expansion]
The exact aggregate right-hand-side perturbation must preserve L_tilde Δy_hat and ΔL_tilde Δy_hat. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, second exact perturbation expansion]
The O(uε) and O(u^2) terms are part of the theorem and cannot be silently omitted. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.24)-(4.25)]

The distinction between the theorem's introduced A_tilde and the A used in its conclusion must be recorded rather than silently normalized. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 and equations (4.23)-(4.24)]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.5 introduces A_tilde but equations (4.23)-(4.24) and the proof use A without locally binding it.
ambiguities.evidence: The opening reads 'Let A_tilde in R^(n×n) be a pb × pb BLR matrix' and describes solving A_tilde x = v, whereas (4.23) is (A + ΔA)x_hat = v + Δv and (4.24) is measured against ||A||. Section 2.1 earlier uses A_tilde for a BLR representation of A. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Section 2.1; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5 and equations (4.23)-(4.24)]
ambiguities.impact: The natural reading is that A is the original dense matrix represented by A_tilde, but that relationship is inherited rather than stated in Theorem 4.5. A formal contract must not silently replace A with A_tilde or treat them as syntactically identical. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, equations (2.1)-(2.4); PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]

ambiguities.issue: Nonsingularity and the runs-to-completion condition are not repeated in Theorem 4.5.
ambiguities.evidence: The proof invokes Theorems 4.2 and 4.3, each of which assumes A is nonsingular and its algorithm runs to completion. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, Theorem 4.3; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, proof of Theorem 4.5]
ambiguities.impact: Theorem 4.5 cannot be read as guaranteeing a result after factorization breakdown; those conditions are inherited prerequisites. [PDF pp. 19, 21, printed pp. 969, 971, Theorems 4.2-4.3]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.5 refers only to Table 1 for ξ_p and does not restate the detailed compression-scale choices.
ambiguities.evidence: Table 1 labels cases only as local/global and with/without recompressions. The preceding UFC derivation says subsequent bounds use scaled thresholds, while the UCF discussion says such scaling is unnecessary. [PDF p. 17, printed p. 967, equations (4.13)-(4.15); PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1 and Theorem 4.2; PDF pp. 21-22, printed pp. 971-972, Theorem 4.3 and following discussion]
ambiguities.impact: Selecting a ξ_p value requires inheriting the algorithm-specific meaning of local/global threshold; the theorem alone does not fully specify β_ij or intermediate-recompression parameters. [PDF pp. 17, 19, 21, printed pp. 967, 969, 971, cited threshold passages]

ambiguities.issue: Theorem 4.4 displays only the forward block ordering even though Theorem 4.5 also applies it to an upper-triangular solve.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.4 displays T_ii x_i = v_i - sum_(j=1)^(i-1) T_ij x_j. In the proof of Theorem 4.5, the U_tilde solve is introduced only with 'Similarly'. [PDF p. 23, printed p. 973, Theorem 4.4; PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, upper-solve equation]
ambiguities.impact: Standard reverse-order block back substitution is strongly implied, but its exact index formula is not printed in the selected theorem chain. [PDF pp. 23, 25, printed pp. 973, 975, cited solve passages]

ambiguities.issue: The symbols ΔA and Δv are reused for different perturbations during the proof, and the factorization sign convention changes.
ambiguities.evidence: Theorem 4.2 writes A = L_tilde U_tilde + ΔA, while the proof of Theorem 4.5 starts from A + ΔA = L_tilde U_tilde and later names the aggregate perturbations ΔA' and Δv'. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, equation (4.16); PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, proof of Theorem 4.5]
ambiguities.impact: The exact composition must use separately named factorization, solve, and aggregate perturbations. The sign change is harmless for existential norm bounds but matters in a literal symbolic translation. [PDF pp. 19, 24-25, printed pp. 969, 974-975, cited equations]

ambiguities.issue: The big-O remainders are not expanded into explicit finite constants.
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (4.24) and (4.25) end in O(uε) and O(u^2), respectively, while the proof shows the exact cross products but does not give constants for those remainder notations. [PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, equations (4.24)-(4.25) and exact proof expansions]
ambiguities.impact: The source supports an asymptotic bound with retained remainder terms, not a fully explicit inequality obtained by deleting or assigning arbitrary constants to them. [PDF pp. 24-25, printed pp. 974-975, cited bounds]

ambiguities.issue: No pivoting policy is fixed by the theorem.
ambiguities.evidence: The surrounding text discusses pivoting and possible growth, but Theorem 4.5 merely names Algorithms 1 and 2 and retains ||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| in its bound. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, stability discussion; PDF p. 21, printed p. 971, UCF pivoting discussion; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equation (4.24)]
ambiguities.impact: The result is not an unconditional small-error statement independent of factor growth, and no particular partial, rook, or other pivoting variant should be inserted into the contract. [PDF pp. 19, 21, 24, printed pp. 969, 971, 974, cited passages]

contract_plain_english: Under the paper's real floating-point model and truncated-SVD compression assumption, take a p-by-p block problem of block order b, successfully compute BLR LU factors with UFC Algorithm 1 or UCF Algorithm 2, and then compute the two triangular solves. [PDF pp. 3-5, printed pp. 953-955, Sections 2.1-2.2 and Assumption 2.1; PDF pp. 13, 21, 24, printed pp. 963, 971, 974, Algorithms 1-2 and Theorem 4.5] The resulting x_hat admits simultaneous perturbations of the original-matrix symbol A and right-hand side v such that (A + ΔA)x_hat = v + Δv, with the exact bounds (ξ_p ε + γ_p)||A|| + γ_(3c)||L_tilde||||U_tilde|| + O(uε) and γ_p(||v|| + ||L_tilde||||U_tilde||||x_hat||) + O(u^2), where c = b + 2r^(3/2) + p. [PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, equations (4.23)-(4.25)] The coefficient ξ_p is 1, p, p, or p^2/sqrt(6) according to local/global threshold and without/with intermediate recompressions. [PDF p. 19, printed p. 969, Table 1] Before big-O simplification, the proof retains every product of factor and solve perturbations, including ΔL_tilde ΔU_tilde and ΔL_tilde Δy_hat. [PDF p. 25, printed p. 975, exact proof expansions] The source has a genuine notation gap because it introduces A_tilde as the solved BLR matrix but states the final perturbation relation and bounds using A; Section 2.1 suggests A is the underlying original matrix, but Theorem 4.5 does not say so locally. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Section 2.1; PDF p. 24, printed p. 974, Theorem 4.5]
